title: The fibre functor
statement:
In the situation of [def-galois-categories], with $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ understood as finite locally constant sheaves of sets in the sense of Stacks Definition 03RU (etale-locally constant with finite set values), the *fibre functor* is

$$
F_{\bar y}:\mathrm{FLC}(Y)\longrightarrow(\text{finite sets}),\qquad
\mathcal F\longmapsto\mathcal F_{\bar y},
$$

where the stalk is that of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], its finiteness is [lem-galois-flc-set-stalk-finite], and a sheaf morphism is sent to its map on stalks. On $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ the notation $P\mapsto|P_{\bar y}|$ of [def-galois-categories] is used; that the two functors correspond under the identification of [thm-galois-lc-etale] is part of that theorem. Its *automorphism group*

$$
\pi_1(Y,\bar y)=\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar y})
$$

is the group of natural automorphisms of $F_{\bar y}$, embedded into $\prod_{\mathcal F}\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar y}(\mathcal F))$ by evaluation, where the product ranges over the objects of a chosen small skeleton of $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ (one representative of each isomorphism class). Each factor is a finite discrete group by [lem-galois-flc-set-stalk-finite], and $\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar y})$ has the topology induced from their product [def-galois-aut-topology]; this is the *etale fundamental group* of $Y$ at $\bar y$. A $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$-set is a finite set with a continuous action of $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$, and such sets with equivariant maps form the category $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)\text{-}\mathbf{Set}$.
